source.title_on_document: The effects of generative AI usage on employee innovation: Collaboration modes, idea journey, and decline in creative psychological ownership

supplement.where: Appendix A. Supplementary data: 'Supplementary data to this article can be found online at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.technovation.2026.103700' (p. 25)
supplement.holds: Scenario and task materials (Supplement A.1-A.5, incl. DeepSeek interface details), measure details (Supplement B), robustness tables S1-S6 (competing mediators, alternative controls), exploratory process and contextual analyses (Tables S7-S35). No creativity-of-output statistics are referenced anywhere.

paper_design_summary: Four online experiments with Chinese adults and working adults (two vignette experiments, Studies 1-2; two experiments with a live DeepSeek interface, Studies 3-4) manipulate GAI usage intensity (high vs low), human-GAI collaboration mode (GAI-centric, human-centric, symbiotic), or collaborator type (human vs GAI), plus a two-wave field survey of 277 employees (Study 5). Every outcome is self-reported: creative psychological ownership of the idea and intentions to elaborate, champion, and implement it. No study scores the creativity, novelty, or diversity of the ideas participants produced.

studies.label: Study 1 (scenario experiment, 2 x 3 GAI usage x collaboration mode)

assignment.what_was_assigned: One of six written scenarios crossing GAI usage (low vs high) with human-GAI collaboration mode (GAI-centric, human-centric, symbiotic); participants imagined using GAI to draft marketing plans
assignment.quote: A 2 (GAI usage: low vs. high) × 3 (human–GAI collaboration mode: GAI-centric vs. human-centric vs. symbiotic) between-subjects experimental design was employed, resulting in six scenarios (see Supplement A.1). Participants were randomly assigned to one of the six conditions.

arms.name: Six scenario cells (low/high GAI usage x GAI-centric/human-centric/symbiotic)
arms.description: Vignette manipulation only; no participant used an AI tool. Cell sizes not reported.

participants.exclusions: 255 participants screened; those who failed the attention check or failed to recall and describe the task were dropped, leaving 243 valid questionnaires (95.29 percent). The paper does not say whether exclusion happened before or after assignment.
participants.who: Credamo online survey platform users, ages 18-60, mean age 28.09; 51.4 percent male
participants.quote: We then screened the 255 participants based on two criteria: (1) failure of the attention-check test and (2) failure to recall and describe the task. Finally, 243 valid questionnaires remained

ai_tool.name_model: Unnamed GAI described in a scenario
ai_tool.how_used: Imagined only: participants read a scenario about collaborating with GAI to draft marketing plans.

task.description: Read a workplace vignette as a marketing specialist in a cross-border e-commerce company; no creative output produced.

studies.label: Study 2 (scenario experiment, human vs GAI collaborator)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Collaboration partner scenario: an imagined human assistant vs an imagined DeepSeek GAI assistant
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions: human–human collaboration (n = 102) or human–GAI collaboration (n = 98).

arms.name: Human-GAI collaboration
arms.description: Imagined collaborating with DeepSeek as a work assistant to refine a marketing proposal

arms.name: Human-human collaboration
arms.description: Imagined collaborating with a human assistant with similar background

participants.who: Employed adults (mean age 31.83, mean tenure 5.36 years) from manufacturing, retail, IT, public services; recruitment platform not stated for this study
participants.quote: We recruited 200 participants; 41.5% were male, with an average age of 31.83 years (SD = 8.74). The average tenure was 5.36 years (SD = 5.73).

ai_tool.how_used: Imagined only: scenario described DeepSeek generating ideas and revising content while the participant kept final decision authority.

task.description: Read a workplace vignette about jointly refining a marketing proposal; no creative output produced.

studies.label: Study 3 (API-based experiment, high vs low GAI usage)

assignment.quote: Study 3 used a one-factor between-subjects experimental design to examine the effect of GAI usage intensity on employees’ creative psychological ownership. GAI usage was manipulated at two levels: high versus low GAI usage.

arms.name: High GAI usage
arms.description: Required at least five interactions with DeepSeek and at least 60 s on the task page

arms.name: Low GAI usage
arms.description: Required one to two interactions with DeepSeek and at least 20 s on the task page

participants.exclusions: Responses excluded if participants failed to complete the task as instructed, failed manipulation checks, or used external AI tools; the number excluded is not reported.
participants.who: Working adults recruited through Credamo; mean age 31.63, mean tenure 6.37 years
participants.quote: We recruited 188 participants; 37.2% were male, with an average age of 31.63 years (SD = 9.22).

ai_tool.name_model: DeepSeek-V3.2 (thinking mode) via an interface embedded in the survey platform
ai_tool.how_used: Participants chatted with DeepSeek to generate an initial marketing idea for a beverage product and typed the idea into a text box.

arms.description: All cells used DeepSeek; cell sizes not reported

eligibility.reason: Study 4 randomly assigned 305 working adults to six GAI configurations (high vs low usage x collaboration mode) on a marketing-copy task (p. 14, Section 7.2), and Studies 1-2 randomized vignettes; Study 3 does not state random assignment. But every outcome in all five studies is self-reported (creative psychological ownership and intentions to elaborate, champion, implement, on Likert scales). No study rates the creativity, novelty, or diversity of the ideas or copy participants produced, so criterion 3 fails. Study 5 is observational but has no diversity, novelty, or originality outcome, so it does not qualify as observational context either. Belongs in the screening report as 'only outcome self-reported'.

one_line_finding: Higher GAI usage lowered self-reported creative psychological ownership (Study 4: high 3.93, SD .72 vs low 4.12, SD .55, Cohen's d = .30, p. 15; mini meta-analytic estimate -.184, Table 14, p. 22), mainly under GAI-centric collaboration; no creativity of output was scored.
open_questions: Study 3 does not state that the high/low GAI usage conditions were randomly assigned (p. 10-11); only Studies 1, 2, and 4 state random assignment.

Studies 3 and 4 collected the ideas and marketing copy participants produced (entered into a text box), but the paper reports no rating of them; the supplement might hold materials but is not on file.
notes: Outcome lists are left empty because no outcome is scored on the output (form rule 7). Self-reported outcomes in all studies: creative psychological ownership (Baer and Brown 2012, four items), idea elaboration, idea championing, idea implementation intentions, plus alternative mediators (creative self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation, perceived autonomy, idea confidence). No arm in Studies 3-4 works without AI; contrasts are AI configuration vs AI configuration. Study 2 contrasts an imagined GAI partner with an imagined human partner. Funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China and Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province (p. 25); no company involvement stated.
